title: Artificial intelligence and wearable sensors in sports injury risk prediction: current status and future perspectives

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence and wearable sensors in sports injury risk prediction: current status and future perspectives》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Introduction · S0001-p4】In recent years, the rapid development of wearable sensor technologies and AI algorithms has given rise to a new data-driven paradigm for injury risk prediction [13]. Utilizing inertial measurement units (IMUs), surface EMG, heart rate variability (HRV), and emerging flexible bioelectronic sensors, it is now possible to collect high-frequency, continuous, and non-invasive data on athletes’ kinematic, physiological, biochemical, and psychological status during training and competition [14]. At the same time, AI techniques – particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), graph neural networks (GNNs, capable of modeling structured relationships such as joint connectivity), and Transformer-based models – have demonstrated strong capabilities in processing complex, nonlinear, and time-dependent data [15,16]. Through the intelligent mining of multi-modal signals, these algorithms can uncover hidden risk patterns and dynamic trajectories associated with injury onset, enabling precise and personalized risk profiling. The integration of wearable sensing and AI modeling thus represents a major shift from traditional experience-based methods to objective, real-time, and scalable predictive systems, which are increasingly being implemented in professional sports teams, research institutions, and commercial athlete monitoring platforms [17].

【Introduction · S0001-p6】Against this backdrop, this review aims to provide a comprehensive and interdisciplinary overview of recent advances in wearable sensor technologies and AI-driven models for sports injury risk prediction. It seeks to offer a structured, forward-looking reference for researchers and practitioners in sports medicine, intelligent sensing, AI-based modeling, and rehabilitation engineering, while accelerating the translation of predictive technologies into real-world applications across elite sports, clinical rehabilitation, and broader health management domains.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence and wearable sensors in sports injury risk prediction: current status and future perspectives》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Deep learning methods and temporal modeling in injury risk prediction · S0004-S2002-p1】As wearable sensor data become increasingly high-dimensional, heterogeneous, and temporally dynamic, traditional ML models are limited in their capacity to represent sequence-level information and capture complex patterns. In contrast, DL has emerged as a powerful alternative for sports injury risk prediction, offering automatic feature extraction from raw data and superior performance on structured, sequential, and multi-modal inputs. These characteristics make DL architectures particularly suitable for modeling the dynamic training–recovery–adaptation processes observed in real-world sports settings, where injury risk arises from the cumulative interaction of multiple factors over time rather than from isolated events. Importantly, these approaches enable the translation of wearable-derived signals into representations of underlying biomechanical processes, such as dynamic joint stability, neuromuscular coordination, and fatigue accumulation, thereby providing a mechanistic basis for injury risk prediction and supporting more interpretable modeling frameworks.

【Deep learning methods and temporal modeling in injury risk prediction · S0004-S2002-p4】More recently, Transformer architectures, initially developed for natural language processing, have shown promise in modeling long-range dependencies in physiological time series. Their attention-based mechanisms allow for flexible handling of high-frequency sensor streams and multi-week training histories without relying on sequential computation [55]. Pilot studies have explored the integration of IMU data, HRV metrics, and subjective wellness scores into Transformer-based models to generate personalized, temporally aware injury risk forecasts [16].

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Artificial intelligence and wearable sensors in sports injury risk prediction: current status and future perspectives》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · S0007-p1】This review synthesizes recent advancements in wearable sensor technologies and AI algorithms for sports injury risk prediction, highlighting their growing role in transforming athlete monitoring from subjective, intermittent assessments to objective, continuous, and data-driven frameworks. By integrating kinematic, physiological, and psycho-physiological indicators, wearable sensors offer comprehensive insights into biomechanical loading, internal stress responses, and psychological resilience. Concurrently, machine learning and deep learning models – particularly those designed for temporal, multimodal, and biomechanically informed data – have demonstrated strong potential for identifying early warning patterns that precede injury.

【Conclusion · S0007-p2】Together, these developments mark a paradigm shift toward proactive, personalized, and real-time injury prevention. While significant challenges remain, ongoing progress in sensor innovation, interpretable AI, privacy-preserving computation, and digital twin technologies is paving the way for next-generation intelligent monitoring systems. Ultimately, the convergence of AI and wearable sensing has the potential to evolve into an integrated decision-support ecosystem that enhances athlete safety, optimizes training load, and supports long-term performance sustainability across both elite and recreational sports settings.
